```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
set.seed(20250607)
```

ShinyCEA can generate comprehensive, publication-ready reports that
combine all analyses --- deterministic CEA, PSA, VOI, scenarios,
subgroups, BIA, and validation --- into a single Quarto document.
The generated `.qmd` file is fully editable before final rendering
to HTML, PDF, Word, or RevealJS slides.

This vignette demonstrates the full pipeline from model definition
to a complete HTA report.

## The Reporting Pipeline

```
collect_cea_results()     # Deterministic + frontier + tornado
collect_psa_results()     # PSA + CEAC + EVPI/EVPPI
collect_bia_results()     # Budget impact
       |
create_cea_report()       # Write CEA section
create_psa_appendix()     # Write PSA section
create_bia_report()       # Write BIA section
       |
render_hta_report()       # Assemble all + render
```

## Quick Start: One-Command Report

```{r quick, eval = FALSE}
library(ShinyCEA)
m <- cea_sick_sicker()

# Generate a complete report (Quarto .qmd file)
render_hta_report(
  m,
  wtp = 100000,
  n_psa = 1000,
  scenarios = list(
    "Base case" = list(),
    "No discounting" = list(d_cost = 0, d_qaly = 0)
  ),
  title = "Sick-Sicker CEA Report",
  author = "ShinyCEA",
  format = "html",         # also: "pdf", "docx", "revealjs"
  output_dir = "my_report",
  render = TRUE             # set FALSE to edit .qmd first
)
```

This produces `my_report/report.qmd` with all figures in `my_report/figures/`,
and (if `render = TRUE`) the rendered HTML.

## Step-by-Step: Building a Report Manually

### 1. Collect Deterministic Results

```{r collect-cea}
library(ShinyCEA)
m <- cea_sick_sicker()

cea <- collect_cea_results(m, m$default_params(), wtp = 100000)
```

The collected object contains formatted tables and ready-made plots:

```{r tables}
# Publication-ready base-case table
cea$tables$base_case
```

```{r incremental}
# Incremental comparison table
cea$tables$incremental
```

```{r frontier}
# Frontier plot
cea$plots$frontier
```

### 2. Collect PSA Results

```{r collect-psa}
psa <- collect_psa_results(m, m$default_params(), cea$det,
                           wtp = 100000, n_psa = 500)
```

```{r psa-table}
psa$tables$psa_summary
```

```{r ceac}
psa$plots$ceac
```

```{r evpi}
psa$plots$evpi
```

### 3. Collect BIA Results

```{r collect-bia}
strats <- m$info()$strategies
n <- length(strats)
cur <- stats::setNames(rep(1/n, n), strats)
new_mix <- cur
new_mix["std"] <- 0
new_mix["t4"] <- new_mix["t4"] + cur["std"]

bia <- collect_bia_results(m, m$default_params(),
                           population = 50000,
                           current_mix = cur,
                           new_mix = new_mix,
                           years = 5)
bia$plots$waterfall
```

### 4. Assemble the Report

Each collector's output can be turned into Quarto markdown sections:

```{r sections, eval = FALSE}
# Each function returns character lines of markdown
cea_lines <- create_cea_report(cea, output_dir = "report_figures")
psa_lines <- create_psa_appendix(psa, output_dir = "report_figures")
bia_lines <- create_bia_report(bia, output_dir = "report_figures")

# Combine manually if you want custom ordering
all_lines <- c(cea_lines, psa_lines, bia_lines)
writeLines(all_lines, "custom_report.qmd")
```

Or use the master orchestrator to do it all at once:

```{r master, eval = FALSE}
render_hta_report(
  m,
  wtp = 100000,
  n_psa = 1000,
  scenarios = list(
    "Base case" = list(),
    "No discounting" = list(d_cost = 0, d_qaly = 0),
    "High cost" = list(drug_t4 = 1400)
  ),
  subgroups = list(
    "Overall" = list(),
    "High risk" = list(p_HS_std = 0.08)
  ),
  bia_config = list(
    population = 50000,
    current_mix = cur,
    new_mix = new_mix,
    years = 5
  ),
  title = "Complete CEA: Sick-Sicker Model",
  author = "Carlos Pineda",
  format = "html",
  output_dir = "full_report"
)
```

## Output Formats

| Format | Use case | Command |
|:-------|:---------|:--------|
| **HTML** | Interactive viewing, self-contained | `format = "html"` |
| **PDF** | Formal submission (via Typst/LaTeX) | `format = "pdf"` |
| **DOCX** | Word editing, track changes | `format = "docx"` |
| **RevealJS** | Presentation slides | `format = "revealjs"` |

### Presentation Mode (RevealJS)

When `format = "revealjs"`, each section becomes a slide. This is
ideal for presenting CEA results to committees:

```{r slides, eval = FALSE}
render_hta_report(
  m, wtp = 100000, n_psa = 0,
  format = "revealjs",
  title = "CEA Results Presentation",
  output_dir = "slides"
)
```

## Editing Before Rendering

The `.qmd` file is standard Quarto markdown. You can:

- **Add narrative text** between sections
- **Remove sections** you don't need
- **Reorder sections** by moving blocks
- **Change figure captions** and table labels
- **Add citations** using a `.bib` file
- **Apply custom themes** via the YAML header

After editing, render manually:

```bash
quarto render my_report/report.qmd
```

## Report Contents

The generated report includes these sections (each optional):

| Section | Included when | Content |
|:--------|:-------------|:--------|
| Model Description | Always | Name, strategies, parameters, WTP |
| Base-Case Results | Always | Cost/QALY/NMB table, frontier plot |
| Incremental Analysis | Always | ICER table vs reference |
| Tornado Diagram | Tornado params exist | One-way DSA |
| Survival Curves | Model returns survival | OS/PFS curves |
| PSA Summary | `n_psa > 0` | Mean (95% CI) table |
| CE Plane | `n_psa > 0` | Scatter plot with WTP line |
| CEAC | `n_psa > 0` | Acceptability curves |
| Expected Loss | `n_psa > 0` | Opportunity loss curves |
| EVPI | `n_psa > 0` | Value of information |
| EVPPI | `n_psa > 0` + draws | Per-parameter VOI |
| Scenario Analysis | `scenarios` provided | Multi-scenario table |
| Subgroup Analysis | `subgroups` provided | Forest plot + table |
| Budget Impact | `bia_config` provided | Annual table + waterfall |
| Parameter Table | Always | Full parameter appendix |
| Validation Summary | Always | Score + pass/warn/fail counts |
